ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

payload.parent_proof_nl:
Fix an integer n > 1 and let x be a real number with 0 <= x < 1. Set m = floor(n x). Then m is an integer and, by definition of the floor function,

m/n <= x < (m+1)/n.

We compare E(n,x) with E(n,m/n). First, since m/n is rational with n(m/n)=m, we have floor(n(m/n)) = m. So

E(n,m/n) = m - sum_{k=1}^n floor(km/n)/k.

Now let 1 <= k <= n. Because x >= m/n and the map t -> floor(t) is nondecreasing, we get

floor(kx) >= floor(km/n).

Therefore, term by term,

floor(kx)/k >= floor(km/n)/k.

Summing over k = 1, ..., n gives

sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k >= sum_{k=1}^n floor(km/n)/k.

Since floor(nx) = m, it follows that

E(n,x) = m - sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k <= m - sum_{k=1}^n floor(km/n)/k = E(n,m/n).

This is exactly the desired inequality.

domain_restrictions: n is an integer with n > 1
x is real and satisfies 0 <= x < 1
m is defined as floor of n times x, hence m is an integer
m divided by n is defined (requires n not equal to 0, satisfied by n > 1)
parent_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every integer n with n > 1 and every real x with 0 <= x < 1, if m is the floor of n times x, then E(n, x) is less than or equal to E(n, m divided by n).
quantifier_order: for all integers n greater than 1
for all real numbers x with 0 <= x < 1
